premises.text: Valuable web data is trapped in HTML pages; most sites lack APIs and creating them requires developers, so access is limited to organizations that can hire engineers
premises.evidence_span: The majority of sites do not have an API, and creating one is complex

premises.text: A no-code data browser lets anyone turn a webpage into a live table/API by showing example rows and columns that the system generalizes
premises.evidence_span: turn any website. into a table of data or an API in a matter of minutes without writing code

premises.text: Extraction patterns become cloud APIs that can be combined so many sites stream into one application call
premises.evidence_span: Combining the API that I just created with other APIs is very easy

premises.text: Data Factory Chrome extension gives anyone access to Import.io's library of pre-built APIs (and requests for ones not yet built) for instant table extraction
premises.evidence_span: The data factory is a chrome extension that will allow anybody to get access to our library of APIs

premises.text: Free tier remains available while the product scales API coverage
premises.evidence_span: It's all free at the moment, and there will always be a free version

value.text: Web data easily accessible to everyone without writing code, opening the full potential of data inside websites
value.evidence_span: data on the web would be easily accessible to everyone

causal_links.evidence_span: without writing code. For the first time ever, data on the web would be easily accessible to everyone
instantly, the data is extracted from the site, formatted, and placed into a table
making data this simple to use, we can finally begin to open the web

notes: Use-case demos (Red Cross, HP) treated as illustrations of P2/P3, not separate premises. User counts and API launch volume treated as traction, not premises. Vision that every website has an API coded as value framing rather than a premise (v1.3.2 §4.1.4).
